clue.text: Finished a beer trip?

definitions.meaning: dead, done for, wrecked: an old RAF phrase for a lost airman
Burton is a beer from Burton upon Trent, so going out for one is a beer trip

explanation.walkthrough: Burton upon Trent is an English brewing town; its beer was once simply called Burton.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means killed or ruined, while literally it describes popping out for a pint of Burton ale.

clue.text: Notably neither sharp nor flat

parts.note: 'Notably' means in terms of musical notes: a note with no sharp or flat sign is in its unaltered state

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Notably' as 'as regards notes' and the clue turns musical rather than describing a person who is neither clever nor dull.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a note that is not raised or lowered by a semitone is called by this term, also meaning unaffected in manner.

clue.text: Compact evergreen male

parts.note: a fir is an evergreen conifer

explanation.surface: A small evergreen shrub that happens to be a male plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact and solid in texture means hard and unyielding to pressure.

clue.text: Collects what's wanted

parts.note: police gather in wanted criminals, and generally one gathers together whatever is needed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanted' carries the police sense of being sought for arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather people or things together into one place, as police do with suspects they are hunting.

clue.text: Refreshment for abstainer in the end carriage

indicators.note: the abstainer is placed in the middle of the carriage word, so 'in' signals a container

parts.note: a bier carries a coffin, the vehicle for the end of life
TT means teetotal, a person who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't drink takes a soft drink in the last coach of the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The end carriage' looks like the last coach of a train; it is the bier carrying the dead. A teetotaller sitting inside it makes an ale, an irony.
explanation.definitionFit: A pint of this hoppy English ale is a drink that refreshes.

clue.text: Vade-mecum for golfers consistently off the fairway?

definitions.text: Vade-mecum for golfers consistently off the fairway?

parts.words: Vade-mecum for golfers consistently off the fairway?
parts.note: a vade-mecum is a handbook; golfers who miss the fairway end up in long grass and need directions there

explanation.walkthrough: The rough is the long grass beside a golf fairway; a vade-mecum is a pocket handbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known series of travel handbooks, read literally as a manual for those always in the long grass beside the fairway.

clue.text: Beasts that get one's rag out

indicators.note: letters let out of their order are put into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: used as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Animals that are made furious by someone's taunts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get one's rag out' sounds like losing one's temper; 'out' is the anagram signal on ONESRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: These are wild asses of Asia, so a kind of animal.

clue.text: Dismissed from the dispatch department?

definitions.meaning: sent away abruptly, told to leave
parcels leaving a dispatch room have been wrapped and posted off

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sent away unceremoniously; literally it describes goods that have been wrapped up and posted.

clue.text: The glitter Hoagy Carmichael made a song about

definitions.text: Hoagy Carmichael made a song about
definitions.meaning: Hoagy Carmichael was an American songwriter whose most famous standard has this title

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a dreamy sparkling quality, and is also the title of Carmichael's 1927 jazz standard.

clue.text: Practice to which America, for example, reverts

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: turning back means the abbreviation is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A custom to which the United States, for instance, returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Established custom or habitual way of doing something is a synonym for practice.

clue.text: Formal request for something to put on

definitions.meaning: a written bid for a job or permission
an ointment or coat of paint applied to a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A request submitted in writing, and also a substance that is applied, as a lotion to skin.

clue.text: Separate duty

definitions.meaning: a verb: to divide or move apart
one's role or share in an undertaking

explanation.definitionFit: To divide is to split apart; a role or share of the work is one's duty in it.

clue.text: Warning that proves unproductive

parts.note: a menace never carried out, one that is lazy or does nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Unproductive suggests idle, the warning a threat.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty menace that is never acted upon: lazy and inactive, it achieves nothing.

clue.text: Nicer suits for one in office with minimal duties

definitions.text: one in office with minimal duties

indicators.note: the letters are exchanged for a new order, so 'for' signals a swap of letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Smarter clothes are handed out to someone in a cushy office job.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange NICERSUITS, signalled by 'for' in the sense of 'exchanged for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post needing little work, and its holder enjoys office without real responsibility.

clue.text: Swift traveller found it rather a bind here

definitions.text: Swift traveller found it rather a bind here

parts.words: Swift traveller found it rather a bind here
parts.note: Jonathan Swift's Gulliver was tied down by tiny people in the first land he reached

explanation.walkthrough: Swift is the author Jonathan Swift, not a speed; 'a bind' is both a nuisance and being literally tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: The island of the six-inch people in Gulliver's Travels, where the hero woke to find himself pinned with threads.

clue.text: The power that gives us airs

indicators.note: a structure that gives yields and changes shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A great nation that makes us feel superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives us airs' sounds like making us snooty; 'gives' signals the anagram of USAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: A world power is a powerful nation, and this vast country is one.

clue.text: Standing reminder of the past

parts.note: an erected structure commemorating history

explanation.definitionFit: A statue or memorial built to commemorate a person or event is a lasting relic of history.

clue.text: Screen-shifter getting incensed

definitions.note: a cryptic definition: the vessel by which a church is filled with incense smoke

indicators.note: something that shifts moves letters around, so the word's letters get a new order

explanation.surface: A stagehand moving scenery flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incensed' seems to mean angry; it means filled with incense.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurible swung in church burns incense, filling the place with fragrant smoke.

clue.text: Surer place in New York for a start in life

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the abbreviation, so 'in' signals a container
to place letters is to set them out anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone more confident finds a spot in Manhattan to begin their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' tells you to rearrange SURER (to URSER), which then goes inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's room or kindergarten is where young ones begin; it also nurtures seedlings.

clue.text: Recommended reading such as the Bible, say

definitions.meaning: the Christian scriptures, often called by this reverent name

explanation.definitionFit: A praised volume worth reading, and the familiar name for Christian scripture.

clue.text: Smooth advice from a bore

definitions.meaning: a borehole drilled to extract petroleum

explanation.definitionFit: An instruction to lubricate generously, and a shaft sunk into the ground to tap petroleum.

clue.text: Regular movement on the beat

parts.note: a pattern of pulse in music or dance, sounding like a police patrol

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the beat' suggests a police officer's round.
explanation.definitionFit: A recurring pattern of strong and weak pulses, the timing of music.

clue.text: Rejected, we hear, all thetime

indicators.note: says the word is recognised by how it sounds when spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: discarded, cast away, tossed in the bin

explanation.surface: Turned down, apparently, at every moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All thetime' is a printing slip for 'all the time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting from start to finish without break means continuously.

clue.text: The family can be about fifty

indicators.note: the tin word goes around the number, so 'about' signals containment

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A household might run to around fifty people.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of related households sharing a common ancestor, as in Scottish kinship groups.

clue.text: One in a clerical capacity

indicators.note: the name sits in the middle of the longer word

explanation.surface: Someone working in an office role.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name stands for any one person, as a crossword convention.

clue.text: Former pupil and high priest at daggers drawn!

definitions.note: plural noun: printed dagger marks, drawn on a page

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
Eli was the high priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: An alumnus and a senior cleric are at loggerheads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At daggers drawn' means hostile; the daggers here are printers' marks drawn in a text.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the printers' dagger symbols used to mark spurious passages or footnotes.

clue.text: Sung in church, I believe

definitions.meaning: a statement of faith chanted in services
the Latin opening word credo means I believe

explanation.definitionFit: The Nicene statement of faith is sung at Mass, and its Latin name credo translates as I believe.

clue.text: How the well-organised combine is run

definitions.text: How the well-organised combine is run

parts.words: How the well-organised combine is run
parts.note: a combine is a business group; a tidy one operates by method

explanation.walkthrough: A combine here is a commercial group, not a harvester.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in a methodical, orderly way according to a plan.
